SIKAPROOF® A+ 12: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: SikaProof® A+ 12, April 2023, Version 06.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/1/sikaproof-a-plus-12.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide SikaProof® A+ 12 where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 06.01).
1.2 Product description. SikaProof® A+ 12 is a polyolefin (FPO) based sheet membrane for below ground waterproofing of reinforced concrete structures. It is loose laid onto prepared substrates or formwork before fixing reinforcement and casting concrete. A special hybrid bonding layer on the membrane forms a permanent bond with the fresh concrete. Overlap joints are sealed using cold-applied tapes or thermally jointed using appropriate heating equipment. The total thickness is 1,75 mm with a membrane thickness of 1,20 mm.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. SikaProof® A+ 12 may only be used by experienced professionals. Damp-proofing, waterproofing and concrete protection for basements and other below ground concrete structures against ground water ingress. Suitable for use on:
    - Reinforced concrete base slabs
    - Reinforced concrete walls with single and double-faced formwork
    - Extension and reconstruction works
    - Prefabricated structures
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.5.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. SikaProof® A+ 12
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: FPO sheet membrane for pre-applied fully bonded below ground waterproofing
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals / certificates.
    - CE Marking and Declaration of Performance to EN 13967 - Flexible sheets for waterproofing - Damp proofing and basement tanking
    - Watertightness of a Surface Sealing System SikaProof® A+ 12 / SikaProof® Tape A+, WISSBAU®, Germany, No. 2018-275-1
    - Watertightness of a Surface Sealing System SikaProof® A+ 12 / SikaProof® Sandwich Tape, WISSBAU®, Germany, No. 2018-276-1
    - Watertightness of a Surface Sealing System SikaProof® A+ 12 / Thermal Jointing, WISSBAU®, Germany, No. 2019-231-1
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - EN 13967: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - EN 1849-2: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Effective thickness (p.2); Product Information > Mass per area (p.2).
    - EN 12691: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Resistance to impact (p.2).
    - EN 12311-2: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Elongation (p.2); Technical Information > Tensile strength (p.2).
    - EN ISO 527-3: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Modulus of elasticity in tension (p.2).
    - EN 1372: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Adhesion in peel (p.2).
    - EN 12317-2: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Joint shear resistance (p.2).
    - EN 1928: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Durability of watertightness against ageing (p.3); Technical Information > Durability of watertightness against chemicals (p.3); Technical Information > Watertightness (p.3).
    - ASTM D5385: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Resistance to lateral water migration (p.3).
    - EN1847: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Accelerated ageing in alkaline environment (p.3).
    - EN1928: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Accelerated ageing in alkaline environment (p.3).
    - EN 1847: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Durability of watertightness against ageing (p.3); Technical Information > Durability of watertightness against chemicals (p.3).
    - EN 13501-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Reaction to fire (p.3).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Pre-applied: Fixed before placing reinforcement and casting concrete
    - Dual bond: Mechanical and adhesive bond with fresh concrete
    - High flexibility and crack-bridging capabilities
    - No lateral water migration between the concrete structure and the membrane system
    - High watertightness tested according to various standards
    - Fully and permanently bonded to the reinforced concrete structure
    - Resistant to aggressive conditions in natural ground water and soil
    - Easy to install with fully adhered joints
    - Temporarily resistant to weathering and UV exposure during construction
    - Can be combined with other approved Sika® Waterproofing / Joint Sealing Systems
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Appearance and colour: Light yellow membrane containing a light grey bonding layer
2.6 Composition.
    | Membrane Layer | Flexible Polyolefin (FPO) |
    | Hybrid Layer | Cement modified polymer |
2.7 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Mass per area: 1,65 kg/m² (-5/+10 %) (EN 1849-2)
    - Resistance to impact: ≥ 400 mm (EN 12691)
    - Modulus of elasticity in tension: ≤ 35 N/mm² (-/+10 %) (EN ISO 527-3)
    - Joint shear resistance: ≥ 100 N/50 mm (EN 12317-2)
    - Service temperature: -10 °C min. / +35 °C max.
    - Watertightness: Pass (Method B, 24 h/60 kPa) (EN 1928)
    - Resistance to lateral water migration: Pass, up to 7 bar (ASTM D5385 Modified)
    - Accelerated ageing in alkaline environment: Pass (28 d/+23 °C); Pass (Method B, 24 h/60 kPa) (EN1847) (EN1928)
    - Durability of watertightness against chemicals: Pass (28 d/+23 °C); Pass (Method B, 24 h) (EN 1847) (EN 1928)
    - Durability of watertightness against ageing: Pass (12 weeks); Pass (Method B, 24 h/60 kPa) (EN 1847) (EN 1928)
    - Reaction to fire: Class E (EN 13501-1)
2.8 Tensile strength.
    | Machine direction | ≥ 750 N/50 mm |
    | Cross direction | ≥ 750 N/50 mm |
    Test method printed: (EN 12311-2 Meth-
    Test method printed: od A)
2.9 Elongation.
    | Machine direction | ≥ 1100 % |
    | Cross direction | ≥ 1100 % |
    Test method printed: (EN 12311-2 Meth-
    Test method printed: od A)
2.10 Adhesion in peel.
    | ≥ 2,00 N/mm | (to concrete after 28 d) |
    Test method printed: (EN 1372)
2.11 System structure. The following system products must be used:
    - SikaProof® A+ 12 sheet membrane
    - SikaProof® Tape A+ self-adhesive tape for internal jointing
    - SikaProof® Sandwich Tape for internal jointing
    - SikaProof® Tape-150 A self-adhesive tape for internal jointing
    - Accessories and complementary products are available to provide detailing and connection solutions.
    Alternative products:
    Ancillary products:
2.12 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Shelf life: 18 months shelf life from date of production
2.13 Packaging.
    | Product | Roll width | Roll length |
    | SikaProof® A+ 12 | 1,00 m or 2,00 m | 20 m |
2.14 Storage conditions. Product must be stored in original unopened and undamaged sealed packaging in dry conditions and temperatures between +5 °C and +30 °C. Store in a horizontal position. Do not stack pallets of the rolls on top of each other, or under pallets of any other materials during transport or storage. Always refer to packaging.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 06.01) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality. SikaProof® A+ 12 membrane must be applied on a sufficiently stable substrate to avoid movement during the construction works. Substrate surface must be smooth, uniform and clean. Large gaps and voids (≥ 12–15 mm) must be filled before membrane installation. Substrate can be damp or slightly wet, ponding water must be avoided. Suitable membrane fixing substrates include:
    - Concrete blinding
    - Formwork
    - Rigid thermal insulation
    - Plywood sheets / forms

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 06.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Effective thickness.
    | Total Thickness (=deff) | 1,75 mm (-5/+10 %) |
    | Membrane Thickness | 1,20 mm |
    Test method printed: (EN 1849-2)
4.3 Equipment.
    - Tape measure
    - Marking pen
    - Razor knife
    - Scissors
    - Pressure roller
    - Clean lint-free cloth
    - Metal straight edge for cutting
    - Protective sheet for cutting
4.4 Application method / tools.
    - Installation procedure
    - Strictly follow installation procedures as defined in method statements, application manuals and working instructions which must always be adjusted to the actual site conditions.
    - Installation method - General
    - After substrate conditions have been fulfilled, the waterproofing membrane is installed by loose laying onto horizontal / inclined substrates or fastening onto vertical substrates. Overlap and transverse joints are sealed using self-adhesive tapes or thermally jointed using appropriate heating equipment.
    - Overlap and transverse joints
    - All overlap and transverse joints must be bonded and sealed either with cold applied SikaProof® Tape A+ or SikaProof® Sandwich Tape. Alternatively, all overlap and transverse joints can be bonded and sealed with SikaProof® Tape-150 A. Further, all overlap and transverse joints can be thermally jointed with appropriate hot air heating equipment.
    - Installation method - Detailing
    - Form all details and connections using the appropriate SikaProof® ancillary products outlined in the Sika® Method Statement: SikaProof® A+.
    - Construction and expansion joints
    - For sealing these types of joints, use additional Sika® Joint Solutions.
    - Inspection and quality control of installation
    - A final inspection before placing concrete must be carried out to ensure the complete membrane system has been correctly installed, any damage repaired, and the surface of the hybrid-bonding layer is clean. Concrete placement
    - Place concrete directly onto or against the membrane within 90 days after installation. Alternatively, concrete must be placed within 30 days after installation when using SikaProof® Tape-150 A.
    - Formwork removal
    - After removing the formwork, all penetrations such as shuttering anchors, any membrane damage and construction joints must be sealed using the appropriate SikaProof® A+ 12 ancillary products or complementary Sika Waterproofing Systems.
    - Backfilling protection
    - After formwork removal and before backfilling. SikaProof® A+ 12 system must be protected with an appropriate protection sheet as soon as possible or at the latest within 90 days.
4.5 Limitations and important considerations. Installation work must only be carried out by Sika® trained, approved or competent contractors experienced in this type of application.
    - Reference must also be made to the Sika® Method Statement: SikaProof® A+ System for more detailed information.
    - Do not install SikaProof® A+ 12 membrane during continuous or prolonged rain, snowfall or sand-storm.
    - The substrate application surface must be clean with no standing water.
    - If SikaProof® A+ 12 is to be applied under wet conditions or temperatures below +5 °C. Exceptions are possible under special circumstances with appropriate precautions. Contact Sika® Technical Services for more information.
    - Additional Sika® Joint Sealing Solutions (minimum SikaSwell®) must be used for connections, around penetrations and for construction and expansion joints.
    - Concrete must be placed within 90 days after membrane system installation. Alternatively, concrete must be placed within 30 days after installation when using SikaProof® Tape-150 A.
    - Adequate concrete quality (mix design and workmanship) is required to achieve optimum adhesion of the membrane system to the concrete.
    - SikaProof® A+ 12 membrane is not permanently UV and weather resistant. Therefore, the membrane system must not be installed on structures where it will be permanently exposed to UV light.
    - After formwork removal, the membrane system (membrane side) must be protected with appropriate protection sheets as soon as possible or at the latest before backfilling or within 90 days after installation.
    - To ensure the most suitable type of membrane is selected for the project, refer to section ‘Project Design’ of the ‘Sika® Method Statement: SikaProof® A+ System’ or contact Sika® Technical Services for more information.
4.6 Further information.
    - Sika® Method Statement: SikaProof® A+
    - Sika® Method Statement - Extension Thermal Jointing: SikaProof® A
    - Sika® Application Manual: SikaProof® A+
    - Sika® Application Guideline - Thermal Jointing: SikaProof® A+

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +5 °C min. / +45 °C max
5.3 Substrate temperature. +5 °C min. / +60 °C max
5.4 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.5):
    - Do not install SikaProof® A+ 12 membrane during continuous or prolonged rain, snowfall or sand-storm.
    - If SikaProof® A+ 12 is to be applied under wet conditions or temperatures below +5 °C. Exceptions are possible under special circumstances with appropriate precautions. Contact Sika® Technical Services for more information.
5.5 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Effective thickness: Total Thickness (=deff) | 1,75 mm (-5/+10 %); Membrane Thickness | 1,20 mm (EN 1849-2)
    - Mass per area: 1,65 kg/m² (-5/+10 %) (EN 1849-2)
    - Resistance to impact: ≥ 400 mm (EN 12691)
    - Tensile strength: Machine direction | ≥ 750 N/50 mm; Cross direction | ≥ 750 N/50 mm (EN 12311-2 Meth- od A)
    - Modulus of elasticity in tension: ≤ 35 N/mm² (-/+10 %) (EN ISO 527-3)
    - Elongation: Machine direction | ≥ 1100 %; Cross direction | ≥ 1100 % (EN 12311-2 Meth- od A)
    - Adhesion in peel: ≥ 2,00 N/mm | (to concrete after 28 d) (EN 1372)
    - Joint shear resistance: ≥ 100 N/50 mm (EN 12317-2)
    - Watertightness: Pass (Method B, 24 h/60 kPa) (EN 1928)
    - Resistance to lateral water migration: Pass, up to 7 bar (ASTM D5385 Modified)
    - Accelerated ageing in alkaline environment: Pass (28 d/+23 °C); Pass (Method B, 24 h/60 kPa) (EN1847) (EN1928)
    - Durability of watertightness against chemicals: Pass (28 d/+23 °C); Pass (Method B, 24 h) (EN 1847) (EN 1928)
    - Durability of watertightness against ageing: Pass (12 weeks); Pass (Method B, 24 h/60 kPa) (EN 1847) (EN 1928)
    - Reaction to fire: Class E (EN 13501-1)
5.6 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.7 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: SikaProof® A+ 12, April 2023, Version 06.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/1/sikaproof-a-plus-12.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety - Regulation (ec) no 1907/2006 - reach. This product is an article as defined in article 3 of regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 (REACH). It contains no substances which are intended to be released from the article under normal or reasonably foreseeable conditions of use. A safety data sheet following article 31 of the same regulation is not needed to bring the product to the market, to transport or to use it. For safe use follow the instructions given in the product data sheet. Based on our current knowledge, this product does not contain SVHC (substances of very high concern) as listed in Annex XIV of the REACH regulation or on the candidate list published by the European Chemicals Agency in concentrations above 0,1 % (w/w).
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
